summary.text: 教 means “teach” or “instruct.” Early analyses associate 攴 with the graph’s action and 爻 with its pronunciation, though accounts disagree about the earliest structure and whether 子 was present.

formation.text: The best-supported account is phonosemantic: 攴 contributes action, while 爻 supplies a sound cue. Some analyses include 子 as the learner, but accounts differ on whether it was present in the earliest form. The transmitted Shuowen analysis describes 敎 as 攴 plus 𡥉 and links teaching with what those above enact and those below imitate; this is an early dictionary analysis, not independent confirmation of the graph’s original construction.

components.text: 攵 is the conventional side form of 攴. In analyses of 教, 攴 contributes action; interpreting it as a teaching implement is a proposal, and the object represented remains unresolved.

The link between visible 孝 and 𡥉 is disputed: one analysis treats 孝 as a later graphic corruption of a form associated with 爻 and 子, while other accounts reject or differ on that relationship. Its graphic history remains unsettled, and the checked sound comparisons do not support 孝 as the early phonetic element.

sound_limitation.text: Modern Mandarin readings differ, and the checked Baxter–Sagart reconstructions do not support 孝 as the ancient sound element; early-form analyses instead identify 爻.

sound.text: These modern Mandarin readings differ and do not establish an ancient sound role for 孝.

components.text: 爻 is identified as the sound element in analyses of early 教. In Baxter–Sagart, the forms share a final sequence but differ in prefixes; in Zhengzhang, they have comparable rhyme sequences and different initials. The marks’ referent and any original object-name remain unresolved.

sound.text: The Taiwan MOE dictionary gives these current Mandarin readings; this pair does not establish the ancient relation.
The Baxter–Sagart forms share a final sequence but differ in their prefixes; they support a proposed relation, not an exact match.
The Zhengzhang forms have comparable rhyme sequences and different initials; they support a proposed relation, not an exact match.

components.text: Some early analyses include 子 as the learner in a teaching-related construction. Other accounts say it was added later, so its place in the earliest structure is uncertain.

history.text: Accounts of early forms differ: some describe 攴, 子, and 爻 together, while another says 攴 and 爻 came first and 子 was added later. A modern proposal reads the right-hand element as 父 in some forms; the accounts do not settle a sequence of visual stages.

Some accounts report 攴+學 in bronze forms and 言 in Warring States manuscripts. Whether forms containing 學 reflect interchange between 教 and 學 is disputed: one account reports them, while another argues the graphs began distinct and were later interchanged.
The transmitted form 敎 is analyzed as 攴 plus 𡥉. Its explanation links teaching with enactment above and imitation below.

uncertainties.text: The earliest component structure and the graphic changes leading to present 孝 remain disputed. The accounts do not settle whether 孝 descends from 爻+子, whether 子 was original, or the direction and date of any change.
爻 is the best-supported sound element in analyses of early forms. Checked Baxter–Sagart readings differ substantially for 教 and 孝; the marks’ referent and any original spoken name remain unresolved.

senses.period: Oracle-bone use reported; absolute date unresolved
senses.text: An oracle-bone occurrence is interpreted as transmit, instruct, cause, or command; personal or place-name uses are also reported. Teaching and instruction appear in reported bronze and Warring States manuscript contexts. These reports do not show whether teaching developed from the name uses or identify the graph’s original meaning.
An oracle-bone context is interpreted as command or cause. Its relation to the teaching sense is unresolved.

senses.period: Bronze and Warring States manuscript uses reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze and manuscript contexts are reported with 教 meaning teaching or instruction. They do not establish a fully dated path from the reported oracle-bone uses.
A historical dictionary records the sense “school,” but no dated example establishes when it arose.
A dictionary records “admonition”; its chronology and relation to teaching are unresolved.
Doctrine and religious teaching are recorded meanings, but their development from the teaching sense is not dated here.
“Class” is listed as a current gloss, but no contextual example or history is supplied.

limitations.text: The accounts do not establish a complete dated sequence, a transition from reported name uses to teaching, or the development of school, admonition, doctrine, and class senses. These meanings are therefore left unconnected.

overview.text: 教 means “teach” or “instruct.” Early analyses give 攴 a role associated with action and 爻 a sound role; accounts differ on whether 子 belonged to the first construction or was added later.

components.text: 攵 is the side form of 攴 and contributes action; interpreting it as a teaching implement is a proposal.
The link between visible 孝 and 𡥉 is disputed: one account proposes a later graphic corruption, while other accounts reject or differ on that relationship.
爻 is proposed as an early sound element for 教. The displayed current readings do not establish that ancient relationship; historical comparisons are similar but not exact.
Some early analyses include 子 as the learner; others say it was added later.

relationships.text: 攵 contributes action in analyses of 教.
孝 is visible in the present graph, but its semantic or phonetic role and its relation to the earlier left-side form remain disputed.
Early-form analyses identify 爻 as a phonetic component, supported by the cited Old Chinese comparisons.
Some early-form analyses include 子 as the learner; other accounts say it was added later.
